about: READ-ONLY: the brewery tenant's footprint in the production database as one JSON document (infra/forge/tenant-census.sh) — (a) exact row count per table, (b) rows the brewery seed owns per table, matched by the seed's OWN ids/codes read from the checkout's examples/brewery/{seeds,data}/* and never a typed list, (c) jobs/steps and every table carrying a partition or job_id column by partition (real|simulated|shadow), the rest listed as unknown, (d) REAL jobs/steps whose owner_id / subject_id / assignee_id / completed_by is a brewery seed row, counts and the first 20 ids, (e) the workflows table by owning_team with open-job counts. Exit 4 is 'cannot answer' naming the query, never a smaller document that looks whole. Filed for the cutover (ffc83387; David 2026-09-16 'Let's do it'), which evicts the brewery's reference data and trims the simulated packets and must REFUSE if any real packet references a row it would delete — nothing could measure that: the APIs answer per-service and per-actor, the dev pod cannot exec into the cluster, and a port-forward to the prod database is the never-test-against-prod trap (backlog d07dcc2b). The eviction verb takes its bounds from these same queries. Read through the same kubectl + kubeconfig resolution as delete-orphan-object, exec'ing psql in the postgres container the manifest declares, every session opened with SET default_transaction_read_only = on; nothing mutated. Its own timeout: ~130 tables counted exactly plus five docker+kubectl round trips exceed the runner's 30s default.
